resources.string: Find personal data and secrets, score prompt-injection signals, run a policy and guard a model call. The real library runs over the shared contract fixtures; nothing leaves your device.
Sample: %1$s. Double tap to choose another.
Every change runs the library again. Nothing is validated here: the library decides.
This sample has checks the toggles cannot show (a classifier, a canary, a second check of one kind, a given mapping or another order), so the verdict here can differ from its recorded one.
No personal data or secrets found in this text.
Each finding and signal is underlined, with a glyph and its kind beside it.
Each finding replaced by a reversible placeholder, as the library writes it.
This text is very long or has very many findings, so it is shown without highlights, cut to its first %1$d characters. The lists show the first %2$d entries.
Switch checks on to build a policy. The library validates it and runs it on the text above.
Injection scoring is a lexical heuristic: it can miss a paraphrase and flag harmless text. The scanners miss names and addresses. These are signals, not a defence.
The canary appears in the text.
The canary does not appear in the text.
The classifier did not flag the text.
The model is scripted and this sample cannot be edited. What you see is the library result for the contract fixture, as the harness produced it.
Personal data replaced by placeholders; system messages untouched.
Nothing was sent: the call never happened.
The reply was not checked: the call did not get that far.
No text is returned: the call was blocked.
The call failed before it returned a result.
Blocked: an input check blocked the request.
Blocked: an output check blocked the reply.
The policy is not valid, so no verdict was computed.
A classifier check needs a classifier and none was given.
The provider returned an invalid reply.
The detectors run on each labelled sample; precision, recall and F1 compare the spans that were expected with the ones that were found.
The set is small and deliberately contains misses and false positives, so the figures are not a benchmark.
%1$s: precision %2$s, recall %3$s, F1 %4$s; expected %5$d, found %6$d, correct %7$d
%1$s over all kinds: precision %2$s, recall %3$s, F1 %4$s
Every expected or found span, marked correct, missed or extra.
Fixtures live in contracts/guardrails and are shared with the TypeScript implementation. The model is scripted and no classifier is called: nothing leaves your device.

Classify an image and detect the objects in it. The library prepares the input and reads the outputs; a recording of real models, or a model running on this device, supplies the raw numbers. Nothing leaves your device.
Could not load the demo assets: %1$s
Sample image: %1$s. Double tap to choose another.
Recorded replays the raw outputs captured once from the ONNX models. The preprocessing, the geometry and the results are computed here, live.
Real model runs the TFLite models on this device with LiteRT. They are the same families as the recording but not the same weights.
The real models are not in this build. Download them with scripts/vision-models.mjs (--runtime tflite) and build the app again.
Your image has no recording, so it always runs the real model.
Your image needs the real model, which is not in this build. Download it with scripts/vision-models.mjs (--runtime tflite) and build the app again.
Real model unavailable, showing the recording
What is in the picture? The model scores every ImageNet class and the library turns the scores into a ranked list.
Where are the objects? The library decodes the boxes of the model and maps them back to pixels of your image.
The picture as the model sees it after preprocessing, %1$d by %2$d pixels.
Timings: preprocess %1$s ms, inference %2$s, postprocess %3$s ms.
Off by default: the SSD models already suppress overlapping boxes.
The image has no detected boxes.
No detections above the score threshold.
The models are small and make mistakes; the crowd, the panorama and the low-contrast samples show it. The contract covers the plumbing, not the accuracy of a model.
Preprocessing, decoding and box mapping come from the vision library; its fixtures live in contracts/vision and are shared with the TypeScript implementation.
The model output is not valid: %1$s

A small chat that uses the modules together: the context window keeps the conversation inside a budget, guardrails redact personal data and block injection attempts, and the providers retry and fall back. The mock works offline.
Offline and deterministic. The third call is rate limited on purpose, so you can see the retry in the trace.
The gateway at your endpoint, with its own key and free limits.
The same gateway, with a key of your own.
Unavailable until the endpoint is valid
Worker and My key need a gateway endpoint. Type one to enable them; the demo adds /v1/complete.
Not allowed. Use an https:// address with no user, query or fragment; plain http is accepted only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and 10.0.2.2, for development.
The demo posts to this address followed by /v1/complete.
Your key is sent to the gateway in a request header and is never stored. It stays in memory only while My key is selected, so it is gone when you pick another backend or close the app.
Enter your key to send messages with this backend.
Older messages are dropped to fit this many estimated tokens. The newest message is always kept.
Emails, phones, cards, ids and keys are replaced by placeholders before the call and put back in the reply. Your chat still shows what you typed.
No messages yet. Write one below.

Enter sends the message. With a hardware keyboard, Shift+Enter adds a new line.

Five fixed cases go through the same pipeline against the selected backend and are graded by the evals module. Every case also passes on the mock.

Wiring only: the window, the redaction, the retry, the fallback, the HTTP mapping and the grading all come from the modules; the demo adds the screen and a transport over HttpURLConnection.
Hello! I am a small assistant that runs on this device. Ask me anything and I will answer with a prepared reply.
Thanks for the message. This conversation uses the mock backend, so my replies are scripted and always the same.

I can keep going as long as you like. Try a personal detail such as an email address and look at the trace.
